title: Module 14 Misconception Sort
intro: Decide whether each statement is true, false, or depends. These are the misconceptions that cost students points on exams.

items.s: A regression equation shows that X causes Y.
items.why: It describes prediction. Causal claims depend on the design.

items.s: If r = 0, the best prediction of Y for any X is the mean of Y.
items.why: With no linear relationship the line is flat at the mean of Y.

items.s: A steeper slope means a stronger correlation.
items.why: The slope depends on the units of X and Y. Strength is captured by r.

items.s: The regression line is the best linear predictor in the sense of minimizing squared error.
items.why: That is the least squares principle.

items.s: In simple regression, R squared equals the square of Pearson r.
items.why: For one predictor the two are the same.

items.s: Adding more predictors always improves the prediction of the sample, even if the predictors are meaningless.
items.why: R squared never decreases when predictors are added, which is why adjusted R squared exists.

items.s: Predictions for X values outside the observed range are as trustworthy as those within it.
items.why: Extrapolation assumes the pattern continues without evidence.

items.s: Whether to drop a predictor that is not significant in a multiple regression
items.why: A predictor may be nonsignificant because it overlaps with others. Theory and the purpose of the model matter alongside the p value.
